headline: Octopus says a cyberattack on Nov 27 involved data on about 7,500 customers and 22,000 merchants; cards and balances are safe.
summary: New incident page. Octopus Cards Limited press release of Nov 27 (s001, Tier 1, read in a browser): abnormal activity detected in a cyberattack on the morning of Nov 27 and contained; about 7,500 customers' names and photos involved, some with Automatic Add Value Service bank codes and top-up amounts, no credit card or bank account data; about 22,000 merchants' contact details; cards, Mobile Octopus and Wallet safe to use, no financial loss found, a few features may be temporarily affected; investigation under way and authorities informed; affected customers to be contacted. The Standard (s002) and HK01 (s003) report the release; HK01 adds, on unnamed sourcing, that the police, privacy commissioner and Transport and Logistics Bureau were told (c006, Reported). Main answer Confirmed, filed under hack-stated, on the company's own notice. incident_type breach; no service state, since the company says core services run normally and has not named the affected features. Size Regional. Theory sweep: no Hacker News thread; Reddit refused the request. Photograph: Octopus reader on a Hong Kong bus (CC BY-SA 3.0). Privacy check done: no private people, bylines or handles; the notice's hotline numbers and email addresses are left out.
author: Research agent
